title: Research
text: My research sits at the interface of cement chemistry, transport modelling and data science. The goal is to make cementitious materials both lower in carbon and more predictable over very long service lives.

title: Research
text:
Themes


Low-carbon cement design

Coupling GEMS thermodynamic modelling, machine learning and carbon accounting to search for greener cement recipes with multi-objective optimisation.



Repository barriers

Degradation, diffusion and reactive transport across cement–bentonite–host-rock interfaces for radioactive-waste disposal.



Self-healing UHPC/UHDC

Healing capacity and durability of ultra-high performance concrete under aggressive environments, sustained loads and cracking/healing cycles.



Data-driven materials modelling

Hybrid machine-learning and metaheuristic models, FEniCSx/FEM, HPC workflows and X-ray CT image analysis.

title: Bin Xi
text:
About
I am a postdoctoral researcher in the Laboratory for Waste Management (LES) at the Paul Scherrer Institute, Switzerland. My work brings together thermodynamic modelling, reactive-transport simulation and machine learning to design low-carbon cementitious materials and to understand how cement-based barriers evolve in radioactive-waste repositories.
I obtained my Ph.D. from Politecnico di Milano, where I studied the self-healing and long-term durability of ultra-high performance concrete. Before that, I trained in civil engineering at Shenzhen University and Yunnan Agricultural University.
